clue.text: Small, quiet things brought back into the fold, for example

indicators.note: into says the turned creatures go inside the enclosure word

parts.note: a fold is a sheep enclosure, a pen

indicators.note: brought back says the word for the quiet creatures is read in the return direction

parts.note: mice are proverbially quiet, as in 'quiet as a mouse'

explanation.surface: Small, silent creatures are herded back into a sheepfold, as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quiet things' are mice, as in 'quiet as a mouse'; 'brought back' turns MICE into ECIM, and 'into' puts that inside PEN, after S.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is a single sample or instance shown as typical, so it serves as an illustration.

clue.text: Spicy stuff on Italian starter — or pizza?

parts.note: pepper is a hot seasoning
taken as written

indicators.note: starter means just the opening letter of the word Italian is used

explanation.surface: A query about whether a hot topping on an Italian first course is really a pizza.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy sausage that names a popular pizza variety, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Vegetable burnt, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that a word for burnt is heard rather than read

parts.note: charred means scorched or burnt

explanation.surface: A vegetable that has been overcooked to a crisp.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiss chard is a leafy green vegetable.

clue.text: Before silver turns up, chap has seen different metal

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: turns up, in a down clue, says the symbol for silver is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: different signals the letters of seen are rearranged

explanation.surface: Before a precious metal appears, a man has noticed some other metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' just places MAN ahead of the rest; 'turns up' makes GA from AG, and 'different' rearranges SEEN to NESE.
explanation.definitionFit: Manganese is a hard grey metallic chemical element.

clue.text: Solvent that's incomplete-pile hydrogen on top

parts.note: the pile of a fabric is its nap
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

indicators.note: incomplete says the word that loses its final letter

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A solvent described as a stack of hydrogen sitting atop something unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on top' puts NAP and H above THA, which is THAT with 'incomplete' cutting its last T.
explanation.definitionFit: Naphtha is a flammable petroleum distillate used to dissolve substances like rubber.

clue.text: Doctor hasn't given "yes" to sea air

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of hasn't are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician refuses to give his consent to some fresh sea air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a noun but is a verb meaning tamper with: HASNT becomes SHANT, then 'given' adds Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A shanty is a sailors' work song, an air or tune of the sea.

clue.text: Fly around line from the sun

indicators.note: around says the flying word wraps round the letter for line

parts.note: to soar is to fly high

explanation.surface: An insect buzzing around a line of sunlight.
explanation.definitionFit: Solar describes anything coming from or relating to the sun.

clue.text: George gives gold to religious Biblical character

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
taken as written
pi is crossword slang for pious, religious
Lot is the nephew of Abraham in Genesis

explanation.surface: A man named George donates gold to a devout figure from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George' was RAF slang for an aircraft's automatic pilot, so it is not a person here.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen nicknamed the automatic flight-control system George, a slang term still known from wartime aviation.

clue.text: Pest rises with love for a dance

indicators.note: rises, in a down clue, says the insect word is read upwards

parts.note: a gnat is an annoying insect pest
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A nuisance insect gets up together with love to dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance from Argentina.

clue.text: Country covering Rooney's first injury

indicators.note: covering says the country word goes round the other letter

parts.note: Spain is a European country

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of Rooney's is taken

explanation.surface: A nation responsible for the first injury suffered by the footballer Rooney.
explanation.walkthrough: Wayne Rooney is an English footballer, which makes 'injury' feel like a sports report.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprain is a wrenched ligament, a common joint injury.

clue.text: Father attends old Roman site, ultimately — on which Rome founded?

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
Latin means of ancient Rome

indicators.note: ultimately means take the final letter of site

explanation.surface: A dad visits an ancient Roman location and wonders where the city began.
explanation.walkthrough: The Palatine is one of Rome's seven hills, where legend says Romulus founded the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend places the city's founding on the Palatine Hill, so it is the ground beneath the earliest settlement.

clue.text: Rugby's top man, perhaps, shot round the post

indicators.note: round says the shot word wraps round the post word

parts.note: a header is a shot at goal with the head in football
a mast is an upright pole or post

explanation.surface: A rugby star shoots a ball around the goalpost.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is also a famous English public school, so its 'top man' is its principal, not a player.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief teacher at Rugby School is its head, and the clue's 'perhaps' marks one school as an example.

clue.text: Part of a ship which may turn

indicators.note: which may turn says the answer reads the same in both directions

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A section of a vessel that is able to swing about.
explanation.definitionFit: The poop is the raised deck at the stern of a ship.

clue.text: Part of the meal unfinished, say

indicators.note: say means the word for unfinished is heard spoken

parts.note: coarse means rough, not finely finished

explanation.surface: A dish at dinner left incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: A course is one stage of a meal, such as a starter or dessert.

clue.text: Port where river animal died through force

indicators.note: through says the animal and the letter for died sit inside the force word

parts.note: to ram is to force
an otter lives by rivers

explanation.surface: A harbour where a riverside creature was killed by force.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotterdam is a major Dutch seaport.

clue.text: Such is graceful, with terribly neat stride

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters of neat are jumbled

parts.note: to lope is to run with a long bounding stride

explanation.surface: A graceful creature moving with a very tidy gait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly neat' sounds like praise but 'terribly' rearranges NEAT to ANTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gazelles and their kin are famously elegant animals, so the clue gives an example by quality.

clue.text: Aristotle confused? You can bet on it!

indicators.note: confused says the philosopher's name is mixed up

explanation.surface: A muddled Greek philosopher, and an exclamation of certainty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You can bet on it!' poses as an idiom of certainty, but literally means a betting machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A totaliser, or tote, is a machine for pooled betting on races.

clue.text: Penny hasn't all the ingredients for paella? Very funny

parts.note: rice is the main ingredient of the Spanish dish paella
less means lacking, without

explanation.surface: Penny is missing items for her Spanish rice dish, which is hilarious.
explanation.definitionFit: Priceless, informally, means hilariously amusing.

clue.text: Languid, having lost the record?

parts.note: a list is a record of items
the suffix less means without, having lost

explanation.surface: Someone droopy after losing the record.
explanation.definitionFit: Listless means lacking energy or enthusiasm, lethargic.

clue.text: Pig eats fish and bird

indicators.note: eats says the pig word takes the fish word inside

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
a parr is a young salmon

explanation.surface: A pig consumes fish and a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparrow is a small brown songbird.

clue.text: Bird pecked a little

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
bit, past tense of bite, means pecked

explanation.surface: A bird nibbled at a small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A titbit is a small tasty morsel, a little bit of food.

clue.text: Woman touring old Oxford, perhaps

indicators.note: touring says the woman word goes round the letter for old

parts.note: she refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A woman visiting the historic city of Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford is the city but here it is an Oxford, a lace-up leather style of footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford is a classic lace-up brogue type of footwear, an example of the category.

clue.text: Beast longing to break into laugh?

indicators.note: break into says the longing word goes inside the laugh word

parts.note: ha is a laugh
a yen is a craving or longing

explanation.surface: A craving bursting out as laughter, with a nod to the laughing animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyena is an African carnivore famous for its laugh-like call.

clue.text: Insignificant type diverting millstream

indicators.note: diverting suggests rerouting, so the letters of millstream are redirected

explanation.surface: An unimportant fellow redirecting a millstream.
explanation.definitionFit: A small-timer is a minor operator of little importance.

clue.text: Soak is far from reasonable

definitions.meaning: to soak something in liquid, as tea leaves

explanation.definitionFit: Tea leaves are soaked to brew, and an excessive price is called this, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: For whom flag Hibernian, for a start

definitions.text: For whom flag Hibernian, for a start

parts.note: the yellow flag is a type of iris

indicators.note: for a start means take the opening letter of Hibernian

explanation.surface: A football club's flag and the people it belongs to.
explanation.walkthrough: Hibernian means of Ireland, and Hibernian FC is a Scottish club founded by Irish immigrants.
explanation.definitionFit: Hibernia is the Latin name of Ireland, so Hibernian things belong to its people.

clue.text: Hats, eg, had set off lateral feature

indicators.note: set off suggests starting up afresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an ear sits at the side of the head

explanation.surface: Hats, for example, that once showed off a feature on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eg' looks like part of the definition but is fodder: 'set off' rearranges EG and HAD to HEADG.
explanation.definitionFit: Headgear is the collective term for things worn on the head.

clue.text: Spinner needing rest

definitions.meaning: in snooker, a long-legged cue support

explanation.definitionFit: A web-weaving arachnid shares its name with the snooker player's multi-legged cue support.

clue.text: As an athlete, practise for heat

explanation.definitionFit: Athletes loosen up before an event, and food is reheated, two senses of one phrasal verb.

clue.text: Chief invested in a quarter for campaign fund

indicators.note: invested in says the chief word is placed inside the quarter word

parts.note: west is one quarter of the compass
arch means principal, chief

explanation.surface: A leading figure puts money into a neighbourhood for a campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A war chest is money reserved for a political or military campaign.
